answer: One concrete anti-Sybil defense locks capital: established agents stake a jade-equivalent bond when sponsoring newcomers. The network’s timber of trust expands only via these verified endorsements, and misconduct by a recruit slashes the sponsor’s beacon of collateral. An attacker cannot freely mint identities; each fake requires either tying up scarce funds for the lock period or persuading honest agents to risk their own stake, multiplying the cost linearly with the sybil count.
